solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Religious follower of AC/DC interrupting short beat

indicators.note: interrupting means the slang word breaks into the middle of the shortened beat
short tells us to drop the last letter of the word for beat

parts.note: to baste is to beat or thrash
AC/DC is slang for bisexual, abbreviated BI

explanation.surface: A fan of a heavy rock band disrupting a drummer's clipped rhythm, dressed up as religious devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC wants to be the Australian rock band; here it is slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: A Babist follows the Bab, founder of a nineteenth-century Persian religious movement.

clue.text: Religious follower of AC/DC welcoming newer band

indicators.note: welcoming means the slang abbreviation takes the band's name inside itself

parts.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, abbreviated BI
A-ha is a Norwegian pop band of the 1980s, newer than AC/DC

explanation.surface: A rock fan making room for a younger group, framed as a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC wants to be the band; it is slang for bisexual, and the newer band is the Norwegian group A-ha.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baha'i is an adherent of the faith founded by Baha'u'llah, which grew out of Babism.

clue.text: Monk, dammit, has run inside

indicators.note: inside says the single letter for run goes within the exclamation

parts.note: bother is a mild exclamation of annoyance, like dammit
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The setter, Monk, cursing because he has a run going in his stockings or a cricket run inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Monk is also the setter's own pseudonym, which makes the definition look like a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks are addressed as Brother within religious orders, so the title stands for a member of one.

clue.text: Subdue Joanna, just a little bit

definitions.meaning: to play something down or tone it down
Joanna is rhyming slang for piano, and one small part of a piano is the pedal that makes it quieter

explanation.surface: Telling Joanna to calm down, just slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang (Joanna = piano), not a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal is to play down; the soft pedal is the piano pedal that mutes the tone.

clue.text: By pub fire, finish off wine

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place

indicators.note: finish off means the final letter of the word for fire is removed

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job

explanation.surface: Sitting by the pub fire, polishing off a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish off' looks like drinking up the wine, but it cuts the last letter from SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: They're seen in valuations on a regular basis

definitions.text: They're seen in valuations on a regular basis

indicators.note: on a regular basis tells us to take every other letter of the word valuations

explanation.surface: Something that crops up routinely when things are valued.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth and every other letter of vAlUaTiOnS gives the answer, and cars are indeed often valued.
explanation.definitionFit: Autos is an informal word for motor cars, which are regularly the subject of valuations.

clue.text: Ranges of fancy carpets

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests something elaborate or imagined, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A selection of ornate rugs on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective on carpets but signals rearranging the letters of CARPETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectra are full ranges of something, as in a spectrum of colours or of opinions.

clue.text: Fault-finder starts to identify slight engine knock

parts.note: a critic is someone who finds fault

indicators.note: starts to tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A mechanic diagnosing a faint knocking noise from an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock' looks like an engine noise, but it is the definition, meaning to disparage.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something is to disparage it, an informal synonym for finding fault with it.

clue.text: Hastily communicate hot post of him and her showering

indicators.note: showering suggests things scattered about like drops, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A racy online post about a couple in the shower together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showering' rearranges the letters of HOT POST OF HIM and HER.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot from the hip is an idiom for speaking or acting impulsively without careful thought.

clue.text: Departures from Detroit requiring one cab rank?

indicators.note: rank can mean corrupt or foul, so these letters are spoilt into a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: People leaving Detroit needing a taxi from a cab rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a taxi stand but signals rearranging DETROIT, I and CAB. 'Departures' means departures from the main point.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter dicta are incidental remarks, especially a judge's asides, so they digress from the main subject.

clue.text: Sees rat on crib is writhing around

indicators.note: around tells us the rearranged letters wrap round the word for rat
writhing means twisting about, so the letters of crib and is are rearranged

parts.note: to rat on someone is to shop them, informing to the police

explanation.surface: Someone notices a rat on a baby's cot that is squirming about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sees' is a noun here, not a verb, and 'rat' is a verb (to inform on someone), not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, so sees are the territories over which bishops have authority.

clue.text: Very much like to work independently, not up-front

indicators.note: up-front tells us to take the letter at the front of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone who would love to be a freelancer, but not openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not up-front' looks like a deletion, but 'not' is one of the four words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin can be used adjectively for things closely matching or paired, nearly identical in form.

clue.text: Uncovered student anarchist

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree, standing loosely for a student
red is used loosely for a revolutionary or radical leftist

explanation.surface: A radical student revealed or exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: BA strictly marks a graduate rather than a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Bared means stripped or exposed, a synonym of uncovered in the past-tense sense.

clue.text: A positive contribution would benefit it

definitions.text: A positive contribution would benefit it

parts.words: A positive contribution would benefit it
parts.note: A positive is a blood group, so a donation of that type helps a store of donated blood

explanation.surface: Something helped by any constructive input.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A positive' reads as an adjective phrase but is the blood type A+.
explanation.definitionFit: A store holding donated blood benefits from donations of any blood type, including type A positive.

clue.text: No time for bread and wine? That's a bloomer

indicators.note: No tells us the letter for time is left out of the sacrament

parts.note: the Eucharist is the Christian sacrament of bread and wine

explanation.surface: Skipping communion for lack of time would be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucharis, the Amazon lily, is a flowering plant, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: Distraught UN left eastern beach on which Castro may have stood?

definitions.text: on which Castro may have stood?

indicators.note: distraught means very upset, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left and E for eastern

explanation.surface: A troubled UN pulling out of an eastern shore where the Cuban leader once stood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distraught' rearranges UN, L, E and BEACH. 'left' looks like a verb (the UN departed) but gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban heel is a thick, medium-high shoe heel, something a Cuban leader might plausibly stand on.

clue.text: Put together joint sex lessons without heartless master

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the lessons word goes round the degree

parts.note: co-ed describes co-educational teaching, boys and girls taught together

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the degree abbreviation is removed

parts.note: an MPhil is a Master of Philosophy degree

explanation.surface: Mixed sex education classes run without a cold-hearted headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside, not lacking; 'heartless' removes the middle letter of the degree abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To compile is to gather material into a collection, so compiled means assembled or collected.

clue.text: Essentially, Bishops' Bible adopts other sacred work

indicators.note: essentially points to the heart of the phrase, so take its central two letters

parts.note: alter is the Latin word for other

explanation.surface: A sixteenth-century English Bible taking in some other holy text.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of BISHOPSBIBLE is PS. The Bishops' Bible was a 1568 English translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a book of psalms used in worship, a sacred text.

clue.text: Who confronted British by a ridge?

definitions.text: Who confronted British by a ridge?

parts.note: the oche is the raised line or ridge darts players stand behind

explanation.surface: A history question about the enemy facing British troops at a ridge such as Vimy.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCHE is the throwing line in darts, sometimes a raised strip on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Boche was the derogatory First World War term for German soldiers, who faced the British in the trenches.

clue.text: Crew is evasive about power cut in ship

indicators.note: about means the word for evasive surrounds what follows

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, evasive

indicators.note: cut in means the letter for power is inserted into the word for ship

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it, so man stands for ship here
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A crew being cagey about a power failure aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' as a verb means to staff a ship, so it stands for ship; 'cut in' and 'about' nest the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a body of people working together, as in a ship's company of sailors.

clue.text: Suggestion of European blocking Foreign Aid

indicators.note: blocking means the letter for European sits inside, obstructing the other letters
foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the letters of aid are rearranged

explanation.surface: A proposal that a European country should obstruct overseas aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' rearranges AID into IDA, and 'blocking' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought put forward for consideration, a proposal or notion.

clue.text: Craftsman, perhaps one involved in bigamy?

definitions.meaning: a man on a craft, that is a ship's officer, is one example
a bigamist takes a further spouse, a later partner after the first

explanation.surface: A skilled artisan who happens to have two spouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craftsman' means a man on a craft (a vessel), not an artisan.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer ranking below the first mate on a merchant ship; also a bigamist's later spouse.

clue.text: Result of burning some flags in Georgia

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Flags in the US state or the country of Georgia being burned in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A singe is a slight burn on a surface, a scorch mark left by brief contact with flame.

clue.text: Given time, perhaps dock some material

parts.note: dock is a plant, and perhaps marks it as one example of a weed

explanation.surface: Given enough time, maybe a boat could be moored somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a verb about mooring; it is the broad-leaved plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, originally woven in Scotland, used for jackets and suits.

clue.text: Staying in won't do them any harm

definitions.text: Staying in won't do them any harm

parts.words: Staying in won't do them any harm
parts.note: in cricket a batsman who stays in without getting out keeps his scoring figures from falling

explanation.surface: Advice that staying at home never hurt anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staying in' reads as staying at home, but in cricket a batsman who is 'in' has not been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer's runs divided by dismissals; not getting out cannot lower the figure.

clue.text: Part of ship blown apart by navy shell's content

indicators.note: blown apart by means the ship part is split open with the navy letters set inside

parts.note: the keel is the structural spine running along the bottom of a ship
RN stands for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A vessel hit and destroyed by a naval shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shell' looks like artillery but is a nutshell.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the edible inner seed of a nut, the part found inside its hard casing.

clue.text: Old rock band broadcast what Killers did?

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the airwaves, so we hear the band's name spoken

parts.note: Slade was a 1970s British glam rock band from the Midlands

explanation.surface: A veteran band on the radio, compared with The Killers, a modern rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Killers are a band, but here killers are murderers.
explanation.definitionFit: Killers murder people, and slayed is a past-tense form of slay, to kill.
